title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Quantaco AI - Cost Economics (Follow-up)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Reviewed tokens/sec/$ benchmarks across model variants and configs, validated caching savings and discussed batching-latency tradeoffs. Agreed next benchmarks (prefix-heavy workload + larger batch sizes) and to share a cost model spreadsheet and updated security docs.

Redwood to share updated cost model spreadsheet and per-route token breakdown (Jordan) by 2026-05-22

Schedule technical deep-dive on caching/kv behaviour with Quantaco infra (Sofia + Isha) week of 2026-06-01

Jordan Lee - share cost model spreadsheet + pricing scenarios for Dedicated vs Hosted - due 2026-05-22
Aiden Park - upload 200 sample prompts representative of prod queries to shared drive - due 2026-05-24

transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Aiden Park: yeah aiden here, maya, luis, isha joining from quantaco
[00:10] Jordan Lee: great, jordan from redwood, sofia our se, cam csm. agenda today is cost/unit econ - tokens per second per dollar, caching savings, batching tradeoffs, and next steps
[00:30] Maya Chen: sounds good, we've been running the baseline you sent last week, saw some decent latency but cost is our main concern. want to understand where we can shave $/token

[00:45] Sofia Patel: cool, quick refresh: our last run used opt-13b quantized, batch size 1, no prefix caching. we measured about 1.8k tokens/sec on p3-ish hardware and cost around $0.012 per 1k tokens effective, that was without KV caching and without batching optimizations
[01:10] Luis Ortega: that $0.012 per 1k seems higher than our target, we were hoping for closer to $0.006 for the high-volume routes
[01:20] Sofia Patel: totally. so there are three knobs we recommend: batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization/profile. each has different latency vs cost impacts

[01:40] Jordan Lee: i'll walk through numbers we ran in our lab. note these are approximate - transcription may flip some names. for a mid-sized prompt length (~150 tokens) and completion ~200 tokens:
[01:55] Jordan Lee: - batch 1, quantized opt-13b: ~1.8k tokens/sec, cost run: baseline $0.012/1k tokens

[02:10] Jordan Lee: - batch 4, same model: ~5.5k tokens/sec, cost falls to ~$0.0048/1k tokens due to throughput improvements but p95 latency increases from ~120ms to ~360ms per chunk for tail sensitive routes
[02:30] Jordan Lee: - batch 8: ~9-10k tokens/sec, cost down further to ~$0.0032/1k, but latency p95 hits ~700-900ms so not great for interactive chat paths
[02:50] Aiden Park: okay interesting - so batching really moves the tokens/sec/$ but at clear latency cost. our product tracks p95 strict SLA at 300ms for the assistant, so batch 8 would break that

[03:05] Sofia Patel: correct, which is why we suggest hybrid routing: use small batch sizes or dedicated low-latency pool for routes with SLA, and larger batching for background or non-interactive workloads
[03:25] Isha Rao: curious about caching - you mentioned prefix/KV cache savings. our prompts have a lot of repeating boilerplate (legal headers + user profile). any numbers on savings?

[03:40] Sofia Patel: yes. with prefix caching and KV reuse we saw token reduction of 30-45% on prefix-heavy workloads. in practice that means for the same user flow you generate 30-45% fewer new tokens which linearly reduces cost and improves effective tokens/sec because less compute is used per request

[03:58] Jordan Lee: to add, the caching benefit compounds with batching. if you have many requests sharing the same prefix, the runtime can serve cached KV and only compute the completion tokens - so tokens/sec/$ jumps significantly
[04:15] Maya Chen: any tradeoffs for caching re: memory or cold-starts? our infra is tight on GPU memory

[04:25] Sofia Patel: good point - KV caching increases memory use per model shard. we have quant profiles that let you trade precision for memory (e.g., 8-bit quant), and we can pin a smaller set of hot prefixes into an LRU cache. in our tests, enabling KV cache increased memory footprint by ~10-20% depending on model size and context length
[04:45] Jordan Lee: also note that Dedicated pools allow you to provision larger memory instance types if caching is a priority. that's a cost but often worth it for 30% token savings
[04:58] Luis Ortega: what about model choice? is opt-13b always better cost-wise vs a tuned 6b?

[05:08] Sofia Patel: depends on quality and latency. for many tasks a tuned 6B with aggressive quantization can match quality and run at ~2-3x tokens/sec compared to the 13B at same batch. example: gpt-like-6b quantized gives ~3.5k tokens/sec single-thread and at batch4 reaches ~10k tokens/sec with lower absolute memory
[05:30] Aiden Park: so that might be our sweet spot if quality holds. we have a few prompts where hallucination is sensitive though - want to keep a larger model as fallback

[05:45] Jordan Lee: fallback model routing is easy in the platform - you can route by probability of low-confidence to a larger variant. that does increase cost per such request but keeps overall unit econ good
[06:00] Maya Chen: back to numbers, can you share the tokens/sec/$ formula you used? how are you normalizing across hardware?

[06:10] Sofia Patel: sure. tokens/sec/$ = (observed tokens/sec) / (cost per minute of the instance). in our benchmark we normalized to a CUDA p4d-equivalent price. we also include amortized model load time across multiple requests, and for Dedicated we include reserved capacity amortization in per-minute cost

[06:35] Jordan Lee: practical example we gave in the spreadsheet: with batch4 + KV caching on opt-13b, effective cost dropped from $0.012 to ~$0.0028 per 1k tokens in synthetic hot-prefix workloads - that's ~78% savings - but again depends on prefix reuse rate
[06:58] Isha Rao: wow that's large. what's realistic prefix reuse you see in customer workloads?
[07:05] Sofia Patel: varies - some customers with templated prompts see 40-60% reuse. search/query systems see less. you should give us a sample set and we'll run a reuse analysis
[07:20] Aiden Park: we'll upload 200 sample prompts as requested. one other concern is encryption/KMS performance if we bring Dedicated into our VPC. any penalties?

[07:32] Jordan Lee: KMS calls are async and do not materially impact token throughput once keys are cached. we do initial key fetches on boot which is negligible. for high compliance setups we support HSM integrations but we'd want to review with security
[07:48] Maya Chen: good. also SOC2 related docs - can you resend the updated security pack?
[07:54] Jordan Lee: yes i'll send the security binder and SOC2 report, and cam will include the audit log samples
[08:05] Luis Ortega: CPU/GPU scaling - if we go with Dedicated reserved, how do autoscale and burst capacity affect per-token cost?

[08:14] Sofia Patel: autoscale helps keep latency during demand spikes but reduces some utilization efficiency. Reserved capacity amortizes base cost so steady-state is cheaper; bursts on top are billed at higher incremental rates. our cost model spreadsheet shows blended per-token cost for several utilization scenarios

[08:40] Jordan Lee: note too that continuous batching in the runtime packs smaller requests into micro-batches to smooth throughput - that helps with tokens/sec but can add a small ms of queuing which shows up in p50 not p95
[08:58] Isha Rao: can you run one more benchmark with our prompt set and compare batch1 vs batch4 with KV enabled?
[09:05] Sofia Patel: yep we'll do that. expectation is batch4+KV will be best for cost but we'll preserve a batch1 low-latency pool for the assistant route
[09:20] Aiden Park: pricing ask - what's the delta between hosted and Dedicated for our projected scale (10M tokens/day)?

[09:30] Jordan Lee: rough rule: hosted is simpler but per-token is a bit higher; Dedicated with reserved commit at high utilization can cut per-token cost 30-60% depending on model and caching. i'll include scenarios in the spreadsheet for 10M/day with low/med/high reuse
[09:48] Luis Ortega: also curious about cost attribution per route - can you show per-route token breakdown at the token level?
[09:55] Cam Nguyen: yes our console does token-level breakdown and per-route cost. we'll export a sample dashboard and include per-route p95, tokens generated, and cost allocation
[10:10] Maya Chen: outstanding - any risks you want us to know about before we run bigger benchmarks?

[10:18] Sofia Patel: two main things: memory pressure if you enable aggressive KV caching on larger models; and for extreme batching, tail latency can spike on p95. both are manageable but worth tuning on real prompts

[10:34] Jordan Lee: recap: redwood to run batch1/4/8 tests on both 6B and 13B with customer prompt set, enable KV caching runs, share spreadsheet + security docs, quantaco to upload prompts and infra constraints
[10:48] Aiden Park: good summary. let's target results next week. thanks everyone
[10:53] Jordan Lee: thanks all - i'll put notes and next steps in the calendar invite and follow up with files
[10:58] call ended
